BiblicalUsage: Shabbath is the seventh day set apart from the other six, a day on which no work is done. God gave it first as a gift in the manna week, then wrote it into the commandments as a day to remember and keep holy, and made it a sign between Himself and Israel that He is the LORD who sanctifies them. The word stretches beyond the week itself, covering the Day of Atonement and the sabbath year when the land itself rested, and it even heads the title of Psalm 92, a song for the sabbath day.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Sabbath was made for rest, not for rules. It is a weekly reminder that God provides, that He finished His work, and that His people are not slaves to endless labour. I hold that keeping one day holy still teaches us to trust Him with the other six.
